title: The polynomial ring over a field localized at the origin is regular local of dimension d
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $d\ge0$, $R=k[x_1,\dots,x_d]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\mathfrak p=(x_1,\dots,x_d)\subset R$. Then $\mathfrak p$ is a maximal ideal with $R/\mathfrak p\cong k$, and the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d$ whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by the images of $x_1,\dots,x_d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660): for a maximal ideal m of k[x_1..x_n], m is generated by n elements and dim k[x_1..x_n]_m = n, hence k[x_1..x_n]_m is regular local of dimension n; here m = (x_1..x_d)

proof.text: ($R/\mathfrak p\cong k$, $\mathfrak p$ maximal.) Let $\varepsilon:R\to k$ be the $k$-algebra homomorphism with $x_i\mapsto0$ for all $i$ (evaluation at the origin, universal property of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]); it is surjective since it is the identity on constants. Its kernel is $\mathfrak p$: clearly $\mathfrak p\subseteq\ker\varepsilon$; conversely, writing $f=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^\alpha$, every monomial with $\alpha\ne0$ is divisible by some $x_i$, so $f-c_0\in\mathfrak p$, and $\varepsilon(f)=c_0$; hence $f\in\ker\varepsilon$ implies $f\in\mathfrak p$. So $R/\mathfrak p\cong k$ is a field and $\mathfrak p$ is a maximal ideal, in particular prime. (In the source: $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak m)=k$, all $\alpha_i=0$, $P_i(T)=T$, $f_i=x_i$ and $\mathfrak m=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), proof with m = (x_1..x_d), alpha_i = 0, kappa_i = k, f_i = x_i

proof.text: ($R_{\mathfrak p}$ Noetherian local, maximal ideal generated by the $x_i$.) The field $k$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), and $R=k[x_1,\dots,x_d]$ is a $k$-algebra of finite type (take $\mathfrak a=0$), so $R$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. $\mathfrak p$ is prime (step 1), so $R_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}R$, $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and it is Noetherian as a localization of a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Since $\mathfrak p$ is generated by $x_1,\dots,x_d$, the ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak p$ is generated by the images $x_1/1,\dots,x_d/1$ (an element $\sum_jg_jx_j/s$ of $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ equals $\sum_j(g_j/s)(x_j/1)$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), proof with m = (x_1..x_d), alpha_i = 0, kappa_i = k, f_i = x_i

proof.text: ($\dim R_{\mathfrak p}\le d$.) $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal is generated by the $d$ elements $x_1/1,\dots,x_d/1$ (step 2), so its Krull dimension is at most $d$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators] (Krull's height theorem; in Stacks, Tag 00KQ: $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is an ideal of definition generated by $d$ elements, so $\dim=d(R)\le d$).

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension, line 14521), used in the last sentence 'The lemma follows' of the proof of Tag 00OP

proof.text: (A chain of primes of length $d$ in $R$ below $\mathfrak p$.) For $0\le i\le d$ put $\mathfrak p_i=(x_1,\dots,x_i)\subseteq R$, so $\mathfrak p_0=(0)$ and $\mathfrak p_d=\mathfrak p$. Let $\varepsilon_i:R\to k[x_{i+1},\dots,x_d]$ be the $k$-algebra homomorphism with $x_j\mapsto0$ for $j\le i$ and $x_j\mapsto x_j$ for $j>i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; it is surjective, and its kernel is $\mathfrak p_i$ by the argument of step 1 (every monomial containing some $x_j$, $j\le i$, lies in $\mathfrak p_i$, and the remaining part of $f$ is $\varepsilon_i(f)$). Hence $R/\mathfrak p_i\cong k[x_{i+1},\dots,x_d]$, which is an integral domain since $k$ is [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]; so each $\mathfrak p_i$ is a prime ideal. The inclusions $\mathfrak p_i\subsetneq\mathfrak p_{i+1}$ are strict because $\varepsilon_i(x_{i+1})=x_{i+1}\ne0$, i.e. $x_{i+1}\notin\mathfrak p_i$. So $(0)=\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_d=\mathfrak p$ is a chain of prime ideals of length $d$ contained in $\mathfrak p$ (the source's chain $(0)\subset(f_1)\subset\dots\subset(f_1,\dots,f_n)=\mathfrak m$ with $k[x]/(f_1..f_i)\cong\kappa_i[x_{i+1},\dots,x_n]$, here $f_i=x_i$, $\kappa_i=k$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), proof with m = (x_1..x_d), alpha_i = 0, kappa_i = k, f_i = x_i

proof.text: ($\dim R_{\mathfrak p}\ge d$.) Let $\lambda:R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ be the localization at $W=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Each $\mathfrak p_i$ of step 4 is a prime with $\mathfrak p_i\subseteq\mathfrak p$, i.e. $\mathfrak p_i\cap W=\emptyset$, so $\mathfrak p_iR_{\mathfrak p}$ is a prime ideal of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak p_iR_{\mathfrak p})=\mathfrak p_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso (1)]. Extension preserves inclusions, and the inclusions stay strict because the contractions $\mathfrak p_i\subsetneq\mathfrak p_{i+1}$ differ. So $\mathfrak p_0R_{\mathfrak p}\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_dR_{\mathfrak p}$ is a chain of primes of length $d$ in $R_{\mathfrak p}$, and the Krull dimension of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is at least $d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), proof with m = (x_1..x_d), alpha_i = 0, kappa_i = k, f_i = x_i

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 5, $\dim R_{\mathfrak p}=d$. By step 2, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by the $d=\dim R_{\mathfrak p}$ elements $x_1/1,\dots,x_d/1$, so it is a regular local ring of dimension $d$ by definition [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Together with step 1 this is the statement.

split_report.summary: Split following the proof of Stacks Tag 00OP specialized to m=(x_1..x_d) (kappa=k, f_i=x_i): R/p=k by evaluation at 0 (p maximal); R Noetherian (finite-type over the field k) and R_p Noetherian local with maximal ideal generated by the x_i; dim R_p <= d by the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators (created by a previous worker for this item, checked: ringKrullDim_le_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal at KrullsHeightTheorem.lean:490 and spanFinrank_span_le_ncard_of_finite at SpanRank.lean:169 verified, Stacks 00KQ verified, three kinds of search present); chain (0)<(x_1)<...<(x_1..x_d) of primes since R/(x_1..x_i)=k[x_{i+1}..x_d] is a domain, transported to R_p by the prime correspondence of localization, so dim R_p >= d; conclusion by the definition of regular local ring. Added def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring to stmt_deps (and its bracket in the statement); Mathlib re-checked: RegularLocalRing/Polynomial.lean has regularity of polynomial rings only, no dimension of the localization at the origin.

lean.statement: theorem polynomial_origin_regularLocal (k : Type u) [Field k] (d : ℕ) : ∃ hp : (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k))).IsMaximal, letI : (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k))).IsPrime := hp.isPrime Nonempty ((MvPolynomial (Fin d) k ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k))) ≃ₐ[k] k) ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)))) ∧ ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)))) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ Ideal.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k))))) (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k))) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)))) ∧ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)))) = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin d ↦ algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)))) (X i)))
